dedupe_keys.name: faa terminal area forecast taf for us airports

description: The Terminal Area Forecast (TAF) is the official forecast of aviation activity at US airports prepared by the Federal Aviation Administration. It covers the active airports in the National Plan of Integrated Airport Systems: FAA-towered, contract-towered, non-federal towered and non-towered airports. Forecasts are given for enplanements and for operations by air carrier, air taxi and commuter, general aviation and military users, together with historical activity. The FAA page explains that the TAF stays constant until the next publication, and that for the 2025 TAF the enplanements and commercial operations at airports with more than 100,000 enplanements come from origin and destination passenger-flow models. Coverage: US airports in the national plan. Format and access: a web query application with downloadable tables, plus summary reports and methodology documents on the FAA page, without registration. Licence and cost: free, as US federal government work. Caveats: the forecast is a planning baseline that is not revised between editions, and small-airport forecasts rest on simpler methods than those for large hubs. It supports capacity planning, demand scenarios for airport and air network models, and studies of how disruptions compare with expected traffic. It relates to the FAA air traffic activity data, the BTS T-100 traffic statistics and the FAA aeronautical data records in the catalogue.
